explanation: Brilliant! Hard candies and sugarless gum safely kickstart saliva flow and make the dry mouth much easier to handle.

question: How can you, as a nurse, best figure out if a home care client is feeling socially isolated?

options.A: Measuring the client's blood pressure and heart rate
options.B: Asking who the client interacts with or talks to during the week
options.C: Reviewing the client's past surgical history in the hospital chart
options.D: Checking the expiration dates on the client's kitchen food

explanation: Sometimes the best assessment tool is simply asking! Direct and friendly questions help you see just how much human contact they actually get.

question: Why does an HMO require a formal referral before a patient sees a specialist?

options.A: To give the patient something to do on weekends
options.B: To make it as difficult as possible for sick people to get help
options.C: To ensure the specialist hospital gets less money from the pool
options.D: To control costs and ensure patients see the right expert for their condition

explanation: Gatekeeping prevents patients from bypassing basic clinics for expensive specialist care they might not actually need. [learn more](GST322_U4_T8#GST322_U4_T8_h4)

question: What is the main difference between normal grief and complicated grief?

options.A: Normal grief requires heavy psychiatric medication
options.B: Normal grief has no sadness, only anger and frustration
options.C: Complicated grief remains intense and paralyzing for six months or longer
options.D: Complicated grief only happens after sudden accidental deaths

explanation: While normal grief slowly softens over time, complicated grief stays severe and keeps a person from functioning well past the six-month mark.

question: What does the principle of equity mean in community mobilisation?

options.A: Treating only the village elders during an outbreak
options.B: Fair distribution of health benefits without discrimination
options.C: Building clinics only in big cities
options.D: Giving equal amounts of money to every single adult

explanation: Equity ensures that all members of the community, regardless of status, have fair access to health interventions. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T2#GNS124_U4_T2_h3)

question: What is the most likely cause when fluid leaks constantly around the outside of a drainage tube?

options.A: Normal healing of the deeper muscle layers inside
options.B: The collection bag hanging below the level of the bed
options.C: The patient drinking too much water during the night
options.D: A loose seal or saturation of the current dressing

explanation: Leakage around the tube entry site often happens when the dressing is too full to hold more fluid or when the seal around the tube is compromised. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T14#GNS122_U2_T14_h6)

question: Why is the overuse and misuse of antibiotics a serious public health threat?

options.A: It accelerates the development of dangerous antimicrobial resistance
options.B: It permanently ruins hospital refrigeration and storage units
options.C: It causes patients to develop allergic reactions to all known foods
options.D: It immediately bankrupts national pharmaceutical manufacturing firms

explanation: Spot on! Misusing antibiotics teaches bacteria how to survive them, creating superbugs that are terribly hard to treat later.

question: Which health condition is directly caused by severe protein deficiency linked to poor dietary practices?

options.A: Type 2 diabetes
options.B: Hypertension
options.C: Kwashiorkor
options.D: Peptic ulcer disease

explanation: Kwashiorkor is a severe form of malnutrition caused by lack of protein, often seen when children are fed only starchy foods because of taboos.

question: What is the best way to first respond when a patient bravely tells you about abuse?

options.A: Listen without judgment and reassure the patient
options.B: Advise the patient to ignore the incident and move on
options.C: Tell the patient to confront the abuser immediately
options.D: Question whether the patient might have provoked it

explanation: Spot on! Believing them, listening without blaming, and offering a warm shoulder builds instant trust and safety.

question: A patient with uncontrolled pain has a high heart rate and high blood pressure. Which system is causing this?

options.A: Peripheral nerve degeneration
options.B: Parasympathetic nervous system
options.C: Sympathetic nervous system
options.D: Thyroid hormone failure

explanation: Pain is stressful! It activates the sympathetic 'fight-or-flight' response, releasing hormones that speed up your heart and raise your blood pressure.

question: What exactly is a 'specimen' when you are caring for a patient?

options.A: A sterile instrument used during a surgical procedure
options.B: A prescribed medication dose given during a shift
options.C: A sample of tissue or body fluid taken for laboratory examination
options.D: A written record of the patient daily vital signs

explanation: A specimen is simply any biological sample (like blood or urine) collected from a patient to help run lab tests. You'll be collecting these all the time!

question: About how long is the adult female urethra?

options.A: 12 centimeters
options.B: 4 centimeters
options.C: 20 centimeters
options.D: 30 centimeters

explanation: You've got this! The female urethra is quite short (about 4 cm), which makes catheterization quick, though it also means bacteria have a shorter trip to cause trouble.

question: Why should a nurse check a patient's serum albumin lab result before giving a protein-bound drug?

options.A: To measure the exact body fat percentage
options.B: To see how well the kidneys are making urine
options.C: To determine if there is a bacterial infection
options.D: To check if the patient is at risk for drug toxicity

explanation: Low albumin levels change the balance of bound vs. free drug. Checking this lab value helps you keep the patient safe from unexpected high doses of active medicine.

question: Why does leadership matter for every nurse, even those without a fancy management title?

options.A: Staff nurses are solely responsible for hospital budgeting
options.B: Formal titles are required before a nurse can influence safety
options.C: All nurses must eventually manage a hospital department
options.D: Bedside nurses routinely guide peers and advocate for safe care

explanation: Leadership isn't just about titles! Even as a student or bedside nurse, you lead whenever you guide a colleague or speak up for your patient.

question: When is ibuprofen unsafe to use for fever in a child?

options.A: When the child is over one year of age
options.B: When the fever is lower than 38 degrees Celsius
options.C: When the child has concurrent dehydration or kidney issues
options.D: When the child has a mild ear infection

explanation: Ibuprofen can stress the kidneys, so it's risky to use if a child is already dehydrated or has kidney trouble. Good clinical awareness!

question: What is a major reason why unsafe injections happen in low-resource clinics?

options.A: Having too many nurses on duty at night
options.B: Having way too many sterile water supplies
options.C: Shortages of disposable syringes and safety boxes
options.D: Too many mandatory infection control classes

explanation: When basic supplies run low, healthcare workers are put in tough spots. Advocating for proper supplies is a big part of nursing advocacy.

question: A patient is on strict bed rest. What is the most effective nursing action to prevent bedsores (pressure injuries)?

options.A: Applying thick layers of adhesive bandages over the heels
options.B: Massaging reddened bony prominences vigorously with alcohol
options.C: Repositioning the patient on a regular two-hour schedule
options.D: Turning the patient only once during the night shift

explanation: Turning patients every two hours takes the pressure off bony areas, keeping the skin healthy and intact. Brilliant nursing care!

question: What is the primary reason for the physiological anemia seen during pregnancy?

options.A: Plasma volume increases much more than red blood cell mass
options.B: Red blood cells are actively destroyed at a much faster rate
options.C: Frequent blood tests deplete the iron stores of the mother
options.D: Dietary iron is completely blocked from being absorbed in the gut

explanation: Because plasma volume expands much faster and larger than the actual red blood cell count, the blood becomes more diluted, which registers as a lower hemoglobin concentration. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h1)

question: Why is home health care such an exciting shift in modern nursing?

options.A: It moves professional care from large hospitals back into the community
options.B: It focuses only on domestic chores rather than medical tasks
options.C: It completely replaces the need for doctors and clinics
options.D: It removes all responsibilities from family caregivers

explanation: Spot on! Instead of keeping everyone stuck in hospital wards, home care brings the healing right into the patient's familiar home environment.

question: What does the null hypothesis usually say in a Chi-Square test of independence?

options.A: There is a strong positive correlation between variables
options.B: The observed frequencies equal zero
options.C: The sample size is too small to analyze
options.D: There is no association between the variables

explanation: That's right! The null hypothesis always starts by assuming there is no relationship between the things we are studying—any pattern we see is just by chance.

question: Which of these is a key safety outcome indicator in a hospital setting?

options.A: Rate of patient falls with injury
options.B: Total number of staff on annual leave
options.C: Number of visiting family members per day
options.D: Cost of purchasing new intravenous pumps

explanation: Patient falls with injury tell us directly how well our safety measures are protecting vulnerable patients on the ward.

question: What type of tissue does a somatic reflex target?

options.A: Smooth muscle of blood vessels
options.B: Cardiac muscle
options.C: Endocrine glands
options.D: Skeletal muscle

explanation: Somatic reflexes deal with your voluntary skeletal muscles—the ones that let you move your arms, legs, and body around.

question: What is the main reason for preparing a wet mount during a pelvic exam?

options.A: To measure the exact daily urine output of the patient
options.B: To identify specific microorganisms like yeast or parasites under a microscope
options.C: To drain excess fluid from swollen labial glands
options.D: To check if the patient is pregnant

explanation: A wet mount lets the clinician quickly mix a discharge sample with a drop of fluid and peek under a microscope to spot the tiny culprits (like yeast or trichomonas) causing the trouble.

question: Why must the objectives of an explanatory study be very specific?

options.A: To make sure no other nurse can ever replicate the study
options.B: To ensure the research paper is at least one hundred pages long
options.C: To prevent patients from asking questions about the study
options.D: To help the researcher stay focused on finding direct answers and proper statistics

explanation: Exactly! Specific objectives keep your study tightly focused on testing cause and effect without getting distracted.

question: What is a big plus of using hydrogen peroxide gas plasma compared to older gas methods?

options.A: It works instantly without needing any special packaging
options.B: It can be performed easily using standard washbasins
options.C: It operates at low temperatures and leaves no toxic residue
options.D: It is the cheapest method available for hospital wards

explanation: Gas plasma is gentle on delicate equipment and breaks down into harmless water and oxygen, skipping the long wait for aeration.

question: Why would a healthcare planner choose a Cost-Utility Analysis over a regular Cost-Effectiveness Analysis?

options.A: To calculate only the direct financial profits of a new pharmacy wing
options.B: To evaluate treatments that impact both length of life and patient well-being
options.C: To prove that all medical interventions cost the exact same amount
options.D: To avoid measuring clinical outcomes entirely in hospital settings

explanation: When patient comfort and quality of life matter just as much as living longer, a Cost-Utility Analysis (using QALYs) is the best choice.

question: A patient asks why a food with a high glycemic index can sometimes still be eaten in small amounts. What is the best nursing response?

options.A: The glycemic index only applies to people who do not take insulin.
options.B: Glycemic load looks at actual portion size, so a small serving has less overall impact.
options.C: Small amounts of high GI foods completely cure insulin resistance.
options.D: High GI foods automatically turn into low GI foods if you chew them slowly.

explanation: Glycemic load combines the GI score with the actual amount of food eaten, giving a realistic picture of blood sugar impact. [learn more](GNS227_U6_T012#GNS227_U6_T012_h3)

question: How do adults usually approach learning differently from children?

options.A: Adults memorize facts faster without needing to understand the reason
options.B: Adults have no prior knowledge to connect new concepts to
options.C: Adults rely heavily on their prior life experiences and practical needs
options.D: Adults prefer complete dependence on the teacher for daily direction

explanation: Adults love to connect new lessons to what they've already lived through and want to know how the info helps them right now.

question: Which sign is a major warning flag for child trafficking during a clinic visit?

options.A: The parent asks detailed questions about nutrition
options.B: The child eagerly answers all questions independently
options.C: The child brings complete personal school records
options.D: An accompanying adult refuses to let the child speak alone

explanation: Abusive handlers usually control the child's interactions and speak for them to keep their exploitation hidden.

question: A nurse accidentally pricks her finger with a hollow needle used to draw blood. What is the biggest worry?

options.A: Suffering from severe immediate muscle spasms
options.B: Developing an acute allergic reaction to latex
options.C: Developing localized skin necrosis on the finger
options.D: Exposure to bloodborne pathogens like HIV and Hepatitis

explanation: Hollow needles often hold infected blood inside them, which is why a prick poses a direct threat of viral transmission.

question: According to standard color-coding rules, which bin color is used for infectious waste?

options.A: Yellow with a biohazard symbol
options.B: Bright metallic silver
options.C: Plain black or brown
options.D: See-through clear plastic

explanation: Bright yellow bins marked with the biohazard sign are universally used to warn everyone and collect infectious or pathological waste.

question: Why is it important for nurses to ask about cultural beliefs regarding medicines?

options.A: It allows the nurse to legally rewrite hospital medication formularies
options.B: It replaces the need to check laboratory blood test results in the ward
options.C: It ensures the hospital receives international funding for traditional research
options.D: It helps uncover hidden practices that might affect how the patient takes prescribed drugs

explanation: Understanding cultural perspectives reveals compliance barriers and concurrent therapies that patients might not otherwise mention. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h5)

question: A patient has a blockage in their intestinal lymph vessels (lacteals). Which nutrient absorption will be hit hardest?

options.A: Carbohydrates
options.B: Amino acids
options.C: Water
options.D: Lipids

explanation: Remember that dietary fats are too chunky for regular blood capillaries, so they get packaged and sent straight into the lymphatic lacteals instead!

question: What is the primary goal of health promotion?

options.A: Enabling people to increase control over and improve their health
options.B: Providing free medications to rural communities
options.C: Treating acute diseases in hospital settings
options.D: Isolating individuals with infectious conditions

explanation: Health promotion focuses on empowering individuals and communities to manage and better their overall well-being rather than just curing sickness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h1)

question: Which of these is a major barrier to nursing research in busy hospitals?

options.A: Excessive amounts of free time during shifts
options.B: Too many available financial grants and computers
options.C: Heavy clinical workloads and staffing shortages
options.D: Strict bans on publishing local healthcare data

explanation: Spot on! When nurse-to-patient ratios are high and everyone is exhausted, it's really tough to find the energy or time for research. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h5)

question: Why should a nurse always measure height and weight accurately instead of just guessing?

options.A: Inaccurate numbers can lead to dangerous errors in medication dosing
options.B: Patients get offended if the nurse guesses their size
options.C: Estimated numbers make the patient chart look untidy
options.D: Hospital management requires exact figures for billing purposes only

explanation: Many strong drugs, especially for children and critically ill patients, depend on exact body measurements so you don't accidentally give too much or too little. Great job learning the safety rules!

question: Which infant condition involves high bilirubin levels that can cause brain damage and lead to cerebral palsy?

options.A: Kernicterus
options.B: Birth asphyxia
options.C: Placental abruption
options.D: Infant meningitis

explanation: Kernicterus occurs when severe neonatal jaundice goes untreated, allowing bilirubin to cross into the brain and cause permanent injury. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T4#GNS324_U4_T4_h2)

question: What is the main reason nurses use splints and range-of-motion exercises for bedridden clients?

options.A: To cure underlying brain tissue infections
options.B: To prevent permanent joint contractures
options.C: To eliminate the need for turning the client
options.D: To increase daily urine and stool output

explanation: Moving the joints and positioning them right keeps them flexible and stops muscles from freezing into stiff, awkward positions.

question: Why is it so important for you as a nurse to understand how a community functions?

options.A: To prescribe medications without needing a doctor
options.B: To manage hospital financial budgets and staff salaries
options.C: To understand how daily living conditions affect people's health
options.D: To diagnose rare genetic diseases in hospital laboratories

explanation: Spot on! The environment and everyday resources around your patients shape their health just as much as any medicine you give them.

question: What medical term describes how severe or dangerous a disease is when caused by an infectious agent?

options.A: Contagiosity
options.B: Virulence
options.C: Pathogenicity
options.D: Infectivity

explanation: Think of virulence as the 'punch' a germ packs. It tells us how severe or even fatal the resulting disease can be to the host.

question: What is a major role of Community Health Workers in maternal and child health?

options.A: Replacing professional nurses entirely in district hospitals
options.B: Conducting household visits and referring clients with danger signs to clinics
options.C: Importing foreign medical equipment for government clinics
options.D: Performing complex major surgeries in rural health posts

explanation: You got it! Community health workers bridge the gap by visiting homes, sharing health tips, and sending anyone with danger signs straight to the clinic.

question: Which conflict management strategy involves both sides working together to find a solution that satisfies everyone?

options.A: Collaboration
options.B: Accommodation
options.C: Avoidance
options.D: Domination

explanation: Collaboration focuses on open dialogue and problem-solving to achieve a win-win outcome for all involved parties. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T13#GNS124_U5_T13_h5)

question: Why might a dying patient suddenly become restless, pull at their blankets, or reach into the air?

options.A: Brain changes and internal discomfort can cause terminal delirium
options.B: The patient is experiencing a burst of physical strength
options.C: High oxygen levels in the brain are causing extra activity
options.D: Normal vision is suddenly returning before death

explanation: Terminal delirium is a normal reaction to organ changes, toxin buildup, or hidden discomfort like a full bladder. Identifying this helps us keep the patient peaceful.

question: What is the main job of a Nurse Principal Investigator?

options.A: Distributing meal trays to study participants in the clinic
options.B: Cleaning and sterilizing surgical instruments after research surgeries
options.C: Designing studies, securing funding, and overseeing ethical implementation
options.D: Administering daily bed baths to patients on the surgical ward

explanation: Think of a Principal Investigator as the captain of the study—they plan the project, find financial support, and make sure everything follows ethical guidelines. [learn more](GNS217_U2_T5#GNS217_U2_T5_h2)

question: What happens to most of the developing follicles in the ovary during a typical cycle?

options.A: They turn directly into the corpus luteum
options.B: They migrate into the fallopian tubes
options.C: They all release eggs simultaneously
options.D: They degenerate through atresia

explanation: Even though a group of follicles starts growing each month, only one becomes the champion (dominant) follicle. The rest quietly break down through a natural process called atresia.

question: What happens to a vaccine when the cold chain is broken?

options.A: It becomes stronger and requires a smaller dose
options.B: It changes color but remains completely safe to use
options.C: It loses its potency and fails to protect the patient
options.D: It turns into a dangerous liquid poison immediately

explanation: Temperature exposures outside the recommended range permanently destroy the active components of the vaccine. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T66#GNS214_U1_T66_h1)

question: A mum has strong contractions, but her cervical dilation hasn't changed at all for three hours. What is this called?

options.A: Arrest of dilatation
options.B: Protracted latent phase
options.C: Precipitous delivery
options.D: Normal descent

explanation: Exactly right. When dilation completely halts for two hours or more during active labour, we call it an arrest of dilatation.

question: A nurse treats a high blood pressure patient living in a neighborhood with poor food access. What is the best all-round approach?

options.A: Provide medication while also connecting the patient to local nutritional resources and food programs
options.B: Focus solely on writing prescriptions without discussing the patient's diet
options.C: Tell the patient to only purchase expensive imported foods from distant supermarkets
options.D: Advise the patient to stop eating entirely until their blood pressure normalizes

explanation: Brilliant nursing care! Good treatment means handing out medicine while also helping the patient find practical food support right in their community.

question: What is the primary cause of hereditary conditions?

options.A: Exposure to common bacterial infections
options.B: Changes in the DNA sequence
options.C: Inadequate nutrition during pregnancy
options.D: Poor personal hygiene during childhood

explanation: Hereditary conditions stem directly from genetic mutations or alterations passed down from parents to their offspring. [learn more](GNS311_U1_T15#GNS311_U1_T15_h1)

question: Why is improvisation a valuable skill for a nursing educator working in a resource-limited setting?

options.A: It guarantees that students will pass board exams on the first try
options.B: It replaces the need for clinical hospital postings
options.C: It is always superior to factory-made medical equipment
options.D: It overcomes financial shortages without sacrificing student learning

explanation: Improvisation allows educators to deliver practical, high-quality lessons even when funds for buying commercial teaching aids are limited. [learn more](GST321_U8_T4#GST321_U8_T4_h6)

question: Why does the physical form of a medication matter so much to a nurse?

options.A: It decides the exact colour the patient will see
options.B: It dictates the correct and safe route of administration
options.C: It guarantees that side effects will never occur
options.D: It proves whether the drug is synthetic or plant-based

explanation: The physical form of a drug determines how it must safely enter the body, such as by mouth, injection, or skin application. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T7#GNS125_U2_T7_h1)

question: Which of the following is recognized as a harmful traditional practice?

options.A: Standard immunization schedules
options.B: Routine antenatal blood screening
options.C: Exclusive breastfeeding education
options.D: Female genital mutilation

explanation: Correct! Female genital mutilation (FGM) causes deep physical and emotional trauma, making it a severe form of gender-based violence that nurses must help prevent.

question: Why can a PET scan often detect diseases earlier than other imaging methods?

options.A: It uses a much higher radiation dose than standard diagnostic tests.
options.B: It spots abnormal chemical changes in cells before physical damage occurs.
options.C: It relies on the body's natural magnetic field rather than external machines.
options.D: It examines every single organ in the human body simultaneously.

explanation: Spot on! Cells change how they behave and use energy long before an organ shows visible damage on a regular X-ray or CT scan, letting PET catch problems early.

question: Which of these is NOT a common physical barrier for people with disabilities in public buildings?

options.A: Wide automatic sliding entrance doors
options.B: Absence of functional elevators in multi-story buildings
options.C: Narrow doorways that block wheelchairs
options.D: High staircases without accompanying ramps

explanation: Spot on! Wide sliding doors actually make life easier and more accessible, unlike stairs and narrow doors.

question: What is the main goal of analyzing data collected from a community?

options.A: To hide negative statistics from the local government
options.B: To increase the paperwork burden on student nurses
options.C: To identify concrete community health problems and trends
options.D: To replace the need for physical community visits

explanation: Correct! Data analysis helps turn raw numbers into clear patterns so we can see what health challenges the community is truly facing.

question: A patient has a painful abscess right over the palm of their wrist, dangerously close to major nerves and blood vessels. What should you do first?

options.A: Apply hot compresses and send the patient home
options.B: Start high-dose oral antibiotics without any drainage
options.C: Immediately perform bedside incision and drainage
options.D: Refer the patient for specialized surgical evaluation

explanation: Hands and faces have delicate nerves and blood vessels. Abscesses in these tricky spots are best left to specialists to avoid accidental permanent injury.

question: Why do different health workers come together as a team in community health?

options.A: To address complex health and social needs
options.B: To place full control of care on physicians
options.C: To reduce the number of working nurses
options.D: To lower the cost of running hospital wards

explanation: You've got this! Community health involves many overlapping social and physical issues, so different experts team up to tackle them all together.

question: Which bar chart style places sub-category bars directly on top of each other to show a total?

options.A: Grouped bar chart
options.B: Stacked bar chart
options.C: Simple bar chart
options.D: Scatter plot chart

explanation: A stacked bar chart segments a single bar to show both individual parts and the combined total. [learn more](GNS217_U4_T7#GNS217_U4_T7_h3)

question: Which antibody is small enough to cross the placenta and give the baby temporary immunity?

options.A: IgE
options.B: IgM
options.C: IgA
options.D: IgG

explanation: Correct! IgG is the champion antibody that crosses the placental barrier to give the newborn a helpful head start against infections.

question: Eighteen months after losing her husband, a widow still cannot leave her house, eat well, or talk about him without panicking. What kind of grief is she experiencing?

options.A: Anticipatory grief
options.B: Complicated grief
options.C: Delayed grief
options.D: Normal grief

explanation: When grief stays extreme and stops someone from living their normal life long after a loss, we call it complicated grief.

question: How do alkylating agents mainly damage cancer cells?

options.A: By replacing normal cell wall lipids
options.B: By cross-linking DNA strands to stop replication
options.C: By stimulating rapid immune responses
options.D: By blocking plant-derived microtubules

explanation: You're doing great! Alkylating agents tie up the DNA strands so they cannot pull apart and copy themselves, stopping the cancer from spreading.

question: How does systems theory describe an organization like a hospital?

options.A: As a set of interconnected parts working together
options.B: As a strict government entity that cannot change
options.C: As a collection of completely independent workers
options.D: As a machine that never interacts with the outside world

explanation: Systems theory views organizations as living networks where inputs, processes, and outputs affect every department. [learn more](GST321_U1_T3#GST321_U1_T3_h5)

question: If two strangers get into a physical fight at a busy local market, what type of violence is this considered?

options.A: Intimate partner violence
options.B: Community violence
options.C: Collective violence
options.D: Self-directed violence

explanation: Well done! When violence happens outside the home between people who are unrelated and often don't know each other, we call it community violence.

question: How is a longitudinal study different from a cross-sectional study?

options.A: Cross-sectional studies are always experimental, while longitudinal studies are always observational
options.B: Longitudinal studies use animals, while cross-sectional studies only use human nurses
options.C: Longitudinal studies follow participants over a period, while cross-sectional studies collect data at one single point
options.D: Cross-sectional studies take many years to complete, while longitudinal studies take only one day

explanation: You've got it! Think of a cross-sectional study as a quick one-time photo snapshot, while a longitudinal study is like a video tracking changes over time.

question: What must a nurse researcher obtain before starting any experiment involving human subjects?

options.A: A grant from a pharmaceutical company
options.B: Ethical approval from a review board
options.C: Approval from local newspaper reporters
options.D: Permission to buy new uniforms

explanation: Patient safety and rights must be protected, so an ethics committee must review and approve the study plan first. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h6)

question: What are the two primary functions of the human nose?

options.A: Oxygenation and perfusion
options.B: Digestion and phonation
options.C: Respiration and olfaction
options.D: Filtration and circulation

explanation: The nose primarily functions as an airway for breathing (respiration) and as the sensory organ for smell (olfaction). [learn more](GNS211_U4_T3#GNS211_U4_T3_h1)

question: What is an important nursing duty when giving a wearable device to a patient?

options.A: Writing custom software code to link the device to the hospital
options.B: Calibrating the internal microchips using a sterile surgical kit
options.C: Teaching the patient how to wear, charge, and sync the device
options.D: Replacing the device hardware components whenever the battery dies

explanation: As a nurse, your guidance is key! Patients need to know how to handle, charge, and sync their devices so the data keeps flowing.

question: What happens when DRF drugs are sold way below their replacement cost?

options.A: Higher wages for the hospital dispensing personnel
options.B: Faster delivery of goods from pharmaceutical suppliers
options.C: Increased trust from the community healthcare board
options.D: Depletion of capital and eventual stockouts

explanation: If you sell something for 100 naira but it costs 150 naira to replace it, your fund shrinks a little bit every time. Eventually, your shelves will be totally bare!

question: What is the primary difference in lifespan between a Jadelle implant and an Implanon NXT implant?

options.A: Jadelle lasts for up to five years, while Implanon NXT lasts for up to three years
options.B: Jadelle must be removed every year, while Implanon NXT lasts for ten years
options.C: Jadelle contains estrogen for five years, while Implanon NXT contains pure testosterone
options.D: Jadelle is a single rod lasting two years, and Implanon NXT is a six-rod set

explanation: Jadelle consists of two rods providing five years of protection, whereas Implanon NXT is a single rod rated for three years. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T014#GNS226_U6_T014_h3)

question: Why do community nutrition programs sometimes struggle when they introduce unfamiliar foreign foods?

options.A: Local kitchens are physically unable to cook imported ingredients
options.B: Foreign foods contain no vitamins or minerals whatsoever
options.C: Food is deeply connected to personal identity, comfort, and tradition
options.D: Community members refuse to eat anything that has been grown locally

explanation: Spot on! Food is personal and tied to our comfort and identity. If you ignore local food culture, people naturally won't vibe with it.

question: Why do doctors often value an HPV DNA test even more than a standard Pap smear for early detection?

options.A: It detects the underlying viral cause before cellular changes occur
options.B: It can diagnose other unrelated sexually transmitted bacterial infections
options.C: It provides an exact measurement of the tumor size in centimeters
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for any physical pelvic examination

explanation: Brilliant! An HPV test looks for the actual virus's genetic material. This lets us catch the risk early on, even before the virus has had time to visibly damage the cervical cells.

question: Which group of vitamins is most likely to build up and cause toxicity if a patient takes too many over a long time?

options.A: Fat-soluble vitamins
options.B: B-complex vitamins
options.C: Water-soluble vitamins
options.D: Amino acid supplements

explanation: Vitamins A, D, E, and K love to hang out in body fat and the liver rather than washing out in urine, which means excess amounts can build up and become toxic.

question: What is a major risk for patients taking immune checkpoint inhibitors (immunotherapy)?

options.A: The medication causes immediate permanent sterility in both male and female patients.
options.B: The boosted immune system may attack normal, healthy organs, causing widespread inflammation.
options.C: The drug destroys bone marrow production completely, requiring lifelong platelet transfusions.
options.D: The patient will instantly lose all hair follicles within forty-eight hours of the first dose.

explanation: You got it! Reviving the immune system is great for fighting cancer, but sometimes the revved-up immune cells accidentally attack healthy organs like the lungs or gut.

question: How does family planning directly promote gender equality?

options.A: By making biological differences between men and women disappear
options.B: By giving women control over their reproductive lives so they can pursue education and work
options.C: By ensuring that only women make decisions regarding community finances
options.D: By legally prohibiting men from participating in healthcare discussions

explanation: Fertility control frees women from the cycle of constant childrearing, enabling them to pursue personal and professional goals on equal footing. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h4)

question: What is the main difference between rest and sleep?

options.A: Rest requires medication while sleep happens naturally without help
options.B: Rest is a calm, relaxed state while sleep is an altered state with reduced sensory activity
options.C: Rest only occurs at night while sleep can happen at any time of day
options.D: Rest involves reduced consciousness while sleep maintains full alertness

explanation: Think of rest as simply chilling out while you're still awake and aware. Sleep, on the other hand, is a deeper state where your brain tunes out the world around you so it can recharge. You've got this!

question: What is the term for the process of children learning societal gender roles as they grow up?

options.A: Cellular adaptation
options.B: Socialization
options.C: Genetic mapping
options.D: Physiological maturation

explanation: Well done! Socialization is how we absorb the values, behaviors, and roles of our society through family, school, and community.

question: What is the main reason a nurse uses the Braden Scale when a resident is admitted?

options.A: Measuring the severity of cognitive memory loss
options.B: Determining the level of financial independence
options.C: Evaluating the daily nutritional caloric intake
options.D: Assessing the risk of developing pressure injuries

explanation: Awesome! The Braden Scale is a fantastic, standard nursing tool used to predict and prevent skin breakdown.

question: In which lobe of the brain is the primary auditory cortex located?

options.A: Frontal lobe
options.B: Temporal lobe
options.C: Parietal lobe
options.D: Occipital lobe

explanation: The temporal lobe (sitting right around your temples and ears) is where your brain makes sense of the sounds you hear.

question: What is the medical term when individual cells grow larger in size?

options.A: Atrophy
options.B: Hyperplasia
options.C: Metaplasia
options.D: Hypertrophy

explanation: Think 'hyper' (more/bigger) and 'trophy' (growth). Hypertrophy means the cells are getting bigger, not multiplying!

question: Why is routine mental health check-in so important when caring for pregnant adolescents?

options.A: Mental health issues only appear in pregnant women under age twenty
options.B: Routine screening replaces the need for blood pressure checks
options.C: Hormonal changes in teens completely erase all risk of anxiety
options.D: Young mothers face high rates of social stigma, isolation, and depression

explanation: Correct! Pregnant teens often face heavy judgment and loneliness, making emotional support and regular check-ins a must.

question: Where are Golgi tendon organs found in the body?

options.A: Inside the gray matter of the spinal cord
options.B: Deep inside the main belly of skeletal muscle fibers
options.C: At the junction where muscle fibers blend into tendons
options.D: Directly within the outer layer of the skin surface

explanation: Golgi tendon organs sit right at the meeting point where muscle fibers turn into tendons, putting them in the best spot to feel tension.

question: How do long-term conditions like diabetes mellitus usually affect our special senses over time?

options.A: They cause sudden and permanent total hearing loss within days.
options.B: They immediately destroy taste buds on the surface of the tongue.
options.C: They prevent the brain from processing any sensory information.
options.D: They slowly damage delicate blood vessels supplying sensory organs.

explanation: Over time, high blood sugar in diabetes slowly damages tiny blood vessels (microvascular damage). This is why chronic conditions often lead to gradual vision changes like retinopathy. You've got this!

question: Why must a nurse use a separate measuring cylinder for each patient when emptying drainage bags?

options.A: To stop the plastic containers from wearing out too quickly
options.B: To prevent cross-contamination and spread of infections between patients
options.C: To make measuring the fluid much faster during busy shifts
options.D: To ensure the hospital records look neat and well-organized

explanation: Infection control 101! Using dedicated equipment for every patient keeps germs from hitching a ride across the ward.

question: Why do we make time for psychological support and talking after a traumatic, high-risk birth?

options.A: To guarantee the mother never experiences physical fatigue
options.B: To ensure the infant learns to walk at an earlier age
options.C: To help prevent long-term anxiety and post-traumatic stress disorder
options.D: To replace the need for any physical postpartum examinations

explanation: Birth can sometimes be frightening. Helping mums talk through their experience is a wonderful way to heal emotional scars and prevent long-term anxiety.

question: What is the first thing a birth attendant should check on a delivery kit before opening it?

options.A: The brand name of the manufacturer
options.B: The exact weight of the package
options.C: The expiration date of the kit
options.D: The color of the outer plastic wrapper

explanation: Checking the expiry date ensures that the components inside have not exceeded their safe, sterile shelf life. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h3)

question: A pregnant woman in a low-income community skips her antenatal visits to buy food for her children. What economic factor is primarily driving her decision?

options.A: Macroeconomic surplus
options.B: Out-of-pocket financial barrier
options.C: Brain drain
options.D: Excess health insurance coverage

explanation: Having to choose between basic survival needs like food and paying for medical care highlights the harsh impact of direct out-of-pocket expenses. [learn more](GST322_U3_T7#GST322_U3_T7_h5)

question: How does family planning directly help reduce maternal illness and injury?

options.A: By helping women space pregnancies and avoid closely spaced births
options.B: By eliminating the need for routine antenatal care visits at the clinic
options.C: By curing chronic high blood pressure before conception takes place
options.D: By stopping babies from growing too large inside the womb

explanation: Giving the body time to rest between pregnancies lets a mother rebuild her strength and nutrient stores. Spacing is a powerful tool for safe motherhood!

question: Why do health workers always promote barrier methods like condoms?

options.A: They replace the need for routine clinic check-ups entirely
options.B: They provide dual protection against both STIs and unintended pregnancy
options.C: They act as permanent hormonal regulators for the body
options.D: They guarantee complete immunity against every known human virus

explanation: Condoms are great because they block germs and sperm at the same time, protecting against both infections and pregnancy.

question: Why is the active management of the third stage of labor so important in nursing practice?

options.A: It speeds up the dilation of the cervix
options.B: It prevents preeclampsia from developing postpartum
options.C: It guarantees that the baby will not have jaundice
options.D: It helps prevent excessive postpartum bleeding

explanation: You nailed the final one! Using uterotonics and careful cord traction right after baby arrives is key to keeping postpartum hemorrhage at bay. Great job!

question: You walk into an older patient's living room and see an extension cord stretched tightly across the main pathway. What should you do?

options.A: Instruct the patient to tape the cord down with masking tape.
options.B: Recommend moving the cord out of the pathway to prevent a fall.
options.C: Report the patient to local housing authorities for a safety violation.
options.D: Ignore the cord since it supplies power to a necessary lamp.

explanation: Spot on! Clearing tripping hazards from walkways keeps your patient safe from preventable injuries.

question: What is a very common challenge for clients after prostate surgery?

options.A: Permanent loss of the ability to digest proteins
options.B: Chronic infections of the upper respiratory tract
options.C: Urinary incontinence and erectile dysfunction
options.D: Sudden enlargement of the thyroid gland in the neck

explanation: Because the prostate sits right next to the nerves and muscles controlling urination and erections, surgery here often causes temporary or lasting trouble with both functions.

question: How does filtered bicarbonate cross the cell membrane of the kidney tubule?

options.A: It attaches to carrier proteins designed for glucose transport
options.B: It passes directly through large protein channels in the membrane
options.C: It converts to carbon dioxide and water before crossing
options.D: It is actively pumped across by specialized sodium carriers

explanation: Bicarbonate can't easily cross the membrane on its own because of its charge. So, it cleverly teams up with hydrogen to form gas and water first, which easily slip across!

question: What is the MOST important thing to send along when referring a pregnant woman from her home to the hospital?

options.A: A list of local food recipes
options.B: A written referral note detailing history and treatment
options.C: The family's personal photo album
options.D: Extra clothing for the nurse

explanation: Always hand over a clear referral note so the hospital team knows what you found and what care you've already given.

question: A nurse wants to improve sanitation in a rural village. What is the best first step based on community empowerment principles?

options.A: Hold a town hall meeting to listen to community members discuss their main sanitation concerns
options.B: Write an academic paper about rural hygiene without visiting the village
options.C: Order all residents to clean their compounds under police supervision
options.D: Wait for international donors to build modern public toilets

explanation: Starting with dialogue ensures that the community leads the process and addresses problems they actually care about. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T3#GNS225_U2_T3_h7)

question: Why is having a clear 'case definition' so important when investigating an outbreak?

options.A: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies will donate free drugs to the clinic.
options.B: It stops the infectious agent from mutating into a more dangerous strain.
options.C: It ensures all healthcare workers use the exact same criteria to count and track cases.
options.D: It allows nurses to diagnose patients without needing any formal medical training.

explanation: Brilliant! A clear case definition makes sure everyone is on the same page about what symptoms count, preventing messy or inaccurate data tracking.

question: Which bacteria is the most common culprit behind a bad case of strep throat?

options.A: Group A beta-hemolytic Streptococcus
options.B: Staphylococcus aureus
options.C: Streptococcus pneumoniae
options.D: Pseudomonas aeruginosa

explanation: Group A strep is the well-known troublemaker behind acute throat infections. Catching this early means doctors can prescribe antibiotics to prevent any nasty complications!

question: A patient is worried about her changing body after a hysterectomy. Which goal fits best in her care plan?

options.A: The patient will completely forget her anxiety within two hours
options.B: The nurse will make all decisions regarding her emotional care
options.C: The patient will verbalize feelings about body image changes before discharge
options.D: The patient will refuse to discuss her surgery with anyone

explanation: Brilliant! This goal is realistic, supportive, and lets the patient safely express her emotions regarding surgery.

question: What is one of the biggest reasons survivors of sexual violence hesitate to speak up?

options.A: Fear of social stigma and judgment
options.B: The absence of physical pain or injury
options.C: Immediate recovery of emotional stability
options.D: Complete lack of any health complications

explanation: Spot on! Sadly, many survivors stay quiet because they are afraid of being blamed, gossiped about, or judged by society. As nurses, our clinics must always be safe, judgment-free zones.

question: Which level of the Nigerian healthcare system includes federal teaching hospitals and specialized medical centers?

options.A: Community healthcare level
options.B: Secondary healthcare level
options.C: Tertiary healthcare level
options.D: Primary healthcare level

explanation: Teaching hospitals and federal medical centers operate at the tertiary level to provide advanced and specialized care. [learn more](GNS112_U2_T1#GNS112_U2_T1_h1)

question: How does the body react when you consistently take in fewer calories than it burns?

options.A: It immediately stops producing insulin
options.B: It taps into stored energy reserves
options.C: It increases daily resting bone density
options.D: It permanently shuts down digestion

explanation: You've got it! When energy intake drops, the body naturally looks at its stored fat and glycogen to keep running smoothly.

question: What is the primary purpose of a general physical examination?

options.A: To diagnose complex psychiatric disorders independently
options.B: To replace the need for laboratory diagnostic testing
options.C: To prescribe appropriate pharmacological interventions
options.D: To gather baseline data about a patient's health status

explanation: A general exam is primarily done to establish a baseline of physical health so nurses can track changes over time. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h1)

question: Roughly what percentage of surface contaminants can be removed just by taking off a victim's outer clothes?

options.A: About 80 percent
options.B: Exactly 50 percent
options.C: Only 5 percent
options.D: Nearly 100 percent

explanation: Fascinating fact! Simply stripping off contaminated outer clothing gets rid of the vast majority of harmful chemicals right away.

question: Why must you always teach patients never to stop taking their antipsychotic medications abruptly on their own?

options.A: It permanently ruins the patient's long-term memory
options.B: Sudden cessation can trigger symptom relapse or withdrawal
options.C: The medication will turn toxic inside the stomach
options.D: It immediately causes permanent kidney failure

explanation: Stopping antipsychotics suddenly can shock the brain chemistry, causing psychotic symptoms to roar right back or triggering uncomfortable withdrawal effects.

question: What type of immunity is gained when a patient receives a vaccination against a specific disease?

options.A: Innate immunity
options.B: Natural barrier immunity
options.C: Passive immunity
options.D: Active immunity

explanation: Vaccines stimulate the body's own immune system to produce antibodies and memory cells, creating long-term active immunity. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T95#GNS214_U1_T95_h6)

question: Which group of drugs is most commonly grabbed off the shelf for everyday aches without a prescription?

options.A: Intravenous anesthetics
options.B: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs
options.C: Chemotherapy agents
options.D: Injectable insulin products

explanation: That's right! Pain relievers like ibuprofen (NSADs) are easy to buy over the counter, making them hot targets for misuse when body pains flare up.

question: What is a common management failure that lets unsafe injection habits keep happening?

options.A: Failing to provide safety training and discouraging near-miss reporting
options.B: Requiring doctors to supervise every single routine intramuscular injection
options.C: Enforcing strict handwashing rules during morning shift handovers
options.D: Providing too many sharps disposal containers in medication rooms

explanation: When hospitals punish people for speaking up or ignore close calls, hidden dangers stay on the ward waiting to cause actual harm.

question: What should be the main focus during an MBO performance review meeting?

options.A: Reducing the number of nursing staff on duty
options.B: Debating political topics outside of healthcare
options.C: Finding someone to blame when targets are missed
options.D: Problem-solving and comparing results with original goals

explanation: MBO reviews focus on comparing actual outcomes to set objectives and solving any problems that hindered success. [learn more](GST321_U2_T4#GST321_U2_T4_h7)

question: What is the typical age range for early adolescence?

options.A: 10 to 13 years
options.B: 18 to 21 years
options.C: 6 to 9 years
options.D: 14 to 17 years

explanation: Early adolescence generally covers the ages of 10 to 13, marked heavily by the onset of puberty. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T3#GNS312_U3_T3_h2)

question: What term do qualitative researchers use instead of traditional statistical terms like validity and reliability?

options.A: Trustworthiness
options.B: Numeric accuracy
options.C: Precision testing
options.D: Generalizability

explanation: Well done! Because qualitative work deals with stories and feelings rather than numbers, we check its quality by looking at its 'trustworthiness'.

question: When do you need to run a quality control check with liquid control solution?

options.A: Only when the patient asks
options.B: When opening a new container of test strips
options.C: Once every hour
options.D: After every single patient test

explanation: Whenever you crack open a new batch of strips, run a control test to make sure your meter and the new strips agree.

question: How does a standard pacemaker actually assist the heart muscle?

options.A: By sending tiny electrical pulses to prompt regular contractions
options.B: By pumping blood directly through plastic tubes into the aorta
options.C: By delivering high-energy shocks to restart a stopped heart
options.D: By permanently replacing the heart valves with mechanical gates
